D. Pokharkar and Mrs. Manjusha Jagtap - Ware, Advocates for the Respondents - acquiring body in respective matters.

CORAM : SHAILESH P. BRAHME, J.
 DATE : 07TH NOVEMBER, 2025.

FINAL ORDER :
.
Heard both sides finally.
2. These appeals can be decided by common order.
The issue involved in these appeals is no more res-integra.
The distinct judgments and award passed by the Reference Court are challenged.
Appellants are seeking enhancement of compensation mainly on the ground of parity.
3. The appeals are in respect of acquisition of the lands acquired for Minor Irrigation Tank Sheri, Tq. Jamner.

Notification U/Sec. 4 of the Land Acquisition Act was published on 29th August, 2005 and the award was declared on 20 th October,
2008.

4. Learned counsel Mr. Ajeet Kale appearing for the appellants tenders on record common judgment and award dated 15th October, 2024 passed by this Court in First Appeal No. 729 of 2017 and other connected first appeals.

5. Learned counsels for the respondents submit that by the impugned awards the interest is made payable from the date of notification, which needs to be rectified in view of the judgment of the Full Bench of this Court in the matter of The State of  7 42 fa 813.23 Maharashtra Vs.
Kailash
Shiva Rangari reported in AIR 2016 Bom. 141.

6. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the respondents that a review has been filed in respect of common judgment and order dated 15th October, 2024 especially in respect of modification to the extent of para No. 4 therein.

sentences.text: 5 7. There is no serious dispute that appeals can be decided on the basis of the common judgment referred above.

The coordinate Bench partly allowed the appeals awarding rate of Rs.
12,00,000/- per hector for irrigated land, Rs. 6,00,000/- per hector for jirayat land and Rs. 3,00,000/- per hector for pot kharab and 80% of the valuation report for fruit bearing trees.
8. There is no dispute that L.A.R. No. 892 of 2013 was decided and the rates referred above are fixed by the Reference Court.
The respondent - acquiring body did not prefer to challenge the rates.

Besides that in L.A.R. No. 687 of 2010,
L.A.R. No. 688 of 2010, L.A.R. No. 693 of 2010, L.A.R. No. 102 of 2016, L.A.R. No. 103 of 2016, L.A.R. No. 104 of 2016 and L.A.R.
No. 435 of 2010, the identical rates have been awarded by the Reference Court and accepted by the acquiring body.
The review has been filed seeking correction to para No. 4 of the common order dated 15th October, 2024.
I find that the correction solicited is typographical and marginal.
It does not affect the merits of the matter.
In view of the law laid down in the matter of The State of Maharashtra Vs. Kailash Shiva Rangari (supra), appellants are entitled to receive the interest from the date of award.

sentences.text: It is clarified that they are entitled to receive the rental compensation as permissible in law and as per the prevailing government policy.
It would be open for them to apply for the same independently.
In that view of the matter I pass following order.
ORDER A.
First appeals are partly allowed with proportionate costs.
B. Appellants - claimants be paid following compensation.
I. For irrigated land @ 12,00,000/- per hectare.
II. For Jirayat land @ Rs. 6,00,000/- per hectare.
III. For Pot Kharab @ Rs. 3,00,000/- per hectare.
IV. Value of fruit bearing trees @ 80% of the valuation report submitted in the Reference Court.
C. The above compensation shall be paid along with statutory benefits.
D. Appellants shall be entitled to the interest from the date of award as per law.
E. It would be open for them to claim rental compensation as 9 42 fa 813.23 permissible in law and in view of the prevailing government policy.

I. For irrigated land @ 12,00,000/- per hectare.
II. For Jirayat land @ Rs. 6,00,000/- per hectare.

G. Appellants shall not be entitled to claim interest and statutory benefits for the delayed period as per the orders passed while condoning the delay.
